title: Rollout Ethos: traffic steward and policy expression for safe canary strategies
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a new 'traffic steward' component and a lightweight policy expression language to unify canary/A-B/shadow rollout specs across Redwood runtimes. The steward compiles high-level rollout intents (traffic splits, step schedules, cohort classifiers) into enforcement artifacts consumed by the serving control plane and the console. Goals: reduce operator errors in rollout configuration, make guardrails declarative and testable, and enable automatic rollback when composite health predicates fail.
background: Current canary configuration is scattered across console UI forms, runtime YAMLs, and internal defaults. This leads to divergent interpretations between Hosted and Dedicated runs and frequent human errors (forgotten abort thresholds, inconsistent step durations). We need a canonical, minimal surface for specifying: 1) traffic schedule (percent over time or steps); 2) health signals and predicates (latency p99, error-rate, quality regressions from eval set); 3) cohort scoping (users, routes, regions); 4) rollback/backoff policies. The steward will centralize validation, simulation, and compile targets for runtime executors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Policy expression language (PEL) v0 implemented with support for: percent schedules (step and linear), time windows, cohort selectors, and basic boolean health predicates
2) Traffic steward service exposes REST endpoints: validatePolicy, simulatePolicy, compilePolicy
3) Controller can consume compiled artifacts and execute staged traffic shifts against a canary variant with automatic pause/rollback when predicates cross thresholds
4) Console shows simulation visualizations and highlights potential guardrail violations before apply
5) Integration tests cover at least: schedule edge cases, simultaneous multiple cohort deployments, and predicate-triggered rollback
6) Documentation and quickstart (examples for A/B, shadow + canary) published in Confluence and linked in PR
tasks: Integrate compile output with runtime admission controller (runtime team)
Console: add policy editor + simulation chart (DX team)
End-to-end test harness that replays synthetic traffic and health metrics (QA)
Security review for policy evaluation sandboxing (Security)
Migration guide for existing canaries to PEL (PM)
technical_notes: PEL is intentionally small — expressions compile to a JSON artifact containing: ordered steps (percent, duration), cohort selectors (routeRegex, header, region), signals (metric source, aggregation, threshold) and actions (continue, pause, rollback, notify). Use WASM sandbox for evaluation in the console and a trimmed interpreter in the runtime agent to avoid cross-language runtime dependencies. Simulation will run historical telemetry through compiled guardrail predicates to estimate false positive/negative rollback likelihood.
risks: Overly expressive PEL increases surface area for bugs and security issues when evaluating customer-provided predicates. Runtime evaluation must be deterministic and bounded. Also, migrating existing ad-hoc rollouts to PEL may require one-off migrations for percent calculations historically expressed in console. Need migration tooling and default translation heuristics.
migration_plan: Phase 1: opt-in PEL editor and simulation in Console; Phase 2: compile-only mode where runtime accepts compiled artifacts but console still permits legacy forms; Phase 3: default creation uses PEL; provide autorewrite tool that converts 80% of existing policies to PEL format and flags complex ones for manual review.
observability: Add rollout-trace spans and events: policy_id, step_index, applied_percent, signal_values, action_taken. Expose rollout SLO dashboard and per-policy telemetry for cadence analysis. Add an alert when simulated rollback probability exceeds 5% for production traffic.
test_plan: Unit tests for PEL parser and compiler; fuzzing for predicate expressions; integration smoke that runs a canary in a staging cluster and asserts expected pause/rollback behavior when we inject latency/error signals; load test the steward APIs at 1000 validates/sec to ensure performance.
qa_notes: QA to create scenarios: 1) health metric flapping (should backoff, not immediate rollback), 2) cohort overlap (ensure crowding doesn't overshoot percent), 3) shadow+canary combo where shadow quality alerts should not trigger rollback but should surface in console.
